Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
 T1. Historical report [YES] — reports on pricing decisions already made
 T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ongoing war context implies continued price pressure
 T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
 China has intervened for a third time since the outbreak of the Iran war to cap domestic retail fuel price increases. Gasoline and diesel prices are rising below the mechanistically calculated levels (260 vs 435 yuan/ton for gasoline; 250 vs 420 yuan/ton for diesel), effective Sept 12. Cumulatively, prices are now 19–21% above pre-war levels. The state planner is actively absorbing international oil price shocks to shield the domestic economy, signalling sustained elevated oil prices in the global market as a direct consequence of the Iran war.
